Hi Alice - looping in answers and concrete recommendations. TL;DR: recommend service accounts + short-lived JWTs with automated rotation and optional BYOK for stored secrets. Details below and attached diagram/guide.

Recommended pattern (phase 1: server-side):
- Service accounts per environment (dev/stage/prod) and per service (api-ingest, embeddings, reranker).
- Authenticate using signed short-lived JWTs issued by your identity system; Redwood accepts JWTs exchanged for scoped access tokens. Tokens live for a short period (recommended 15 minutes) to limit blast radius.
- For systems where JWTs are not feasible immediately, scoped API keys with automatic rotation are supported for initial onboarding (we can issue a time-limited API key with enforced scope: embeddings:read, generation:invoke).

Key rotation & revocation:
- We recommend automated rotation at least every 30 days for long-lived keys; short-lived JWT flows reduce the need for aggressive rotation of private keys.
- Redwood supports immediate revocation of active API keys and maintains an audit trail of token usage (per-token usage logs retained per your data retention policy).
- For BYOK: we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for encryption-at-rest of secret material; if you require HSM-backed keys, we can support that under our Private deployment or via a signed contract addendum.

Audit & monitoring:
- Audit logs include: token issuance, token exchange (JWT->access token), token revocations, per-token request counts, and latency metrics.
- Logs can be delivered to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, BigQuery) or accessed via the Redwood Console with RBAC.

Scaling & routing notes for embeddings/reranker:
- Given your burst profile (600 RPS), use these mitigations: 1) client-side batching for embeddings, 2) local caching for repeated vectors, 3) dedicated throughput pool (Redwood Dedicated) or request routing to a higher-capacity shard during processing windows.
- Token rate limits: tokens are rate-limited by policy but can be mapped to capacity pools to avoid client-side rejection.

Implementation examples & SDKs:
- Sample server flow: generate signed JWT -> call /v1/auth/exchange -> receive short-lived access token -> call /v1/embeddings or /v1/generate with Authorization: Bearer <token>. See sample code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fintechco-sample-sdk (attached in links).

Next steps I can take for the technical call:
- Provide a short runbook for key rotation (scripts for AWS KMS + Redwood CLI).
- Walk security with our SRE about audit log retention and SIEM forwarding.
- Propose concrete token lifetimes and a migration plan from scoped API keys to JWTs.

Attachments: integration-architecture-diagram.png (high-level auth flow), redwood-integration-guide.pdf (detailed steps)

If that looks good, can we lock the deep-dive for Thu 2028-07-12 10:00am PT? I’ll add our SRE (Rishi) to the invite if you want him there.

Thanks,
